Maldives Immigration Bill

Sponsor of the bill: Mohamed Dawoodh
North Kulhudhuffushi constituency
[signature]
Date: 8 November 2026

[stamp]

Reason for submitting the bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this bill is to establish a separate civil service named Maldives Immigration to run and oversee immigration matters in the Maldives, and to set out the principles relating to the running of that service; the special and general principles relating to persons coming to the Maldives and persons departing the Maldives; the principles relating to issuing the passports Maldivian citizens need to depart the Maldives and return; the principles relating to granting foreigners permission to come to the Maldives and to stay in the Maldives; and, including the principles to be applied in dealing with persons who do not have permission to come to the Maldives or to stay in the Maldives, to determine and set out the principles and procedures relating to immigration under a robust legal framework.

Chapter One
Introduction and Purpose

Introduction and name
1. (a) This is a law that establishes a separate civil service named Maldives Immigration to run and oversee immigration matters in the Maldives, and sets out the principles relating to the running of that service; sets out the special and general principles relating to persons coming to the Maldives and persons departing the Maldives; the principles relating to issuing the passports Maldivian citizens need to depart the Maldives and return; the principles relating to granting foreigners permission to come to the Maldives and to stay in the Maldives; and the principles to be applied regarding persons who do not have permission to come to the Maldives or to stay in the Maldives.

(b) This law shall be cited as the "Maldives Immigration Act".

(b) Upon the establishment of Maldives Immigration as stated in subsection (a) of this section, all legal responsibilities, obligations, employees, property, resources and agreements of the "Maldives Immigration" that operated under the Ministry of Home Affairs before the commencement of this law shall be transferred to the "Maldives Immigration" created under this law.

8. (a) A person shall be appointed to the post of Controller General of Immigration by the President, on the advice of the Minister.

(b) A person appointed to the post of Controller General of Immigration must possess the following attributes.

Entry into the Maldives
24. A person may enter the Maldives only upon fulfilment of the following.

(a) Having a valid passport or a valid travel document in that person's name; and

(b) If that person is a foreigner, that person not being a person referred to in section 26 of this law.

Entry and departure of foreigners

CHAPTER FOUR
Maldivian Passport

Maldivian Passport
36. (a) A Maldivian passport is an official document issued by the Government of Maldives to Maldivian citizens for international travel.

(b) The following categories of passport may be issued under this Act.

(1) Ordinary passport;

(2) Diplomatic passport;

(3) Official passport.

Making and issuing passports
37. (a) Persons seeking a Maldivian passport shall apply to Maldives Immigration, in accordance with the regulation made under this Act, for a passport of the categories specified in Article 36 of this Act.

(b) Maldives Immigration has the power to collect and process the biometric information of persons applying for a Maldivian passport under subsection (a) of this Article, for the purpose of making the passport.

(c) Maldivian passports shall be issued by the Controller General of Immigration in accordance with this Act.

(d) Maldivian passports issued under this Act shall be designed, in line with international standards, in a manner that contains the security features specified in the regulation made under this Act.

(e) In issuing the categories of passport specified in Article 36 of this Act, the Controller General shall ensure that the following conditions are met:

(1) passports shall be issued only to Maldivian citizens; and

(2) in the case of a diplomatic passport, that passport shall be issued only to persons entitled to diplomatic privileges, or to persons of the rank specified in the regulation made under this Act

persons holding senior posts and the dependants of those persons;

(3) in the case of an official passport, that passport shall be issued, for travel for official purposes of the State, only to persons holding State posts of the rank specified in the regulation made under this Act.

(d) An ordinary passport shall be issued for a period of 5 (five) years.

(e) A diplomatic or official passport shall be issued for the period set out in that passport, as specified in the regulation made under this Act.

(f) A diplomatic or official passport shall be issued solely for use for as long as the official capacity in which that passport was issued to that person continues.

(g) An appropriate fee for issuing passports shall be determined in the regulation made under this Act. The [unclear] of the fee so determined [unclear] the fee determined for an ordinary passport [unclear], [unclear] [unclear] [unclear] appropriate [unclear].

Biometric passport

38. (a) A biometric passport containing a biometric chip specific to the person to whom the passport is issued may be issued under this Act.

(b) The biometric passport specified in subsection (a) of this Article, in line with international standards,

the principles of its design, the security features and other attributes to be included in it and its composition, and all procedures to be followed in issuing a passport shall be specified in the regulation made under this Act.

Holding one passport

39. (a) In issuing a Maldivian passport under this Act, the Controller General shall ensure that the passport is issued only to a person who has not been issued another passport.

(b) Where an official passport has been issued to a person, that passport shall be used only for travel for official purposes. In circumstances where that person uses the official passport, that person's ordinary passport shall be kept in the custody of Immigration.

Withholding passports

40. Where a court order has been issued under the Criminal Procedure Act in relation to a person prohibited from leaving, the Controller General has the power to withhold the passport of the person to whom that order relates, for the purpose of enforcing that order.

Cancelling passports

41. The Controller General has the power to cancel the passport of a person to whom a Maldivian passport has been issued under this Act in the following circumstances:

(a) ceasing to be a Maldivian citizen;

(b) the death of that person;

(c) the passport not being collected within the period determined in the regulation made under this Act for making a passport;

(d) the end of the diplomatic or official status held by a person to whom a diplomatic or official passport has been issued, or that person leaving a State post;

(e) the occurrence of any other circumstance specified in the regulation made under this Act.

Loss of or damage to a passport

42. (a) If a Maldivian passport issued under this Act is lost, or if that passport is stolen, Immigration and the Maldives Police Service shall be informed without delay. And if that passport was lost, or stolen, outside the Maldives, the Maldivian diplomatic mission designated for that country, and the nearest police office in that country, shall be informed.

(b) If a Maldivian passport issued under this Act is damaged, Immigration shall be informed of this without delay.

(c) If a Maldivian passport issued under this Act is lost, or if that passport is damaged, the person to whom the passport was issued may apply to Immigration for a new passport to be made.
